Challenge: Software to monitor astronaut health.

Competences : Dev team, motivés, passionnés d'IA & Space.
summary:
SANS Guardian is an offline-first predictive health and monitoring application designed to safeguard astronauts' vision and mental well-being before, during, and after long-duration space missions. Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) affects roughly 70% of astronauts in microgravity and can cause irreversible vision damage, while isolation and operational stress impact crew performance. 

Using pre-mission baseline data (physiological, nutritional, and psychological metrics), SANS Guardian predicts individual SANS risk and enables early intervention. During flight, crew members log daily symptoms and countermeasure adherence (such as thigh cuffs and B-vitamin protocols) via a hands-free offline medical voice assistant. To overcome deep-space connectivity limits, encrypted telemetry syncs to Earth flight surgeons through a delay-tolerant MQTT radio link, generating comprehensive individual and mission-wide reports upon return.
details:
What it does and how it works

SANS Guardian is an end-to-end, offline-first medical monitoring and predictive health platform designed for astronauts before, during, and after long-duration spaceflights. It addresses two critical human spaceflight challenges: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)—which affects roughly 70% of astronauts—and in-flight mental well-being.

The system operates across four integrated stages:

  1. Pre-Mission Baseline & Risk Prediction: Over a defined pre-flight period (e.g., 60 days), the app collects baseline physiological, ocular, nutritional (B-vitamin status), genetic, and psychological data. Using a predictive machine learning model, it estimates each astronaut's individual susceptibility to developing SANS or cognitive fatigue in microgravity.
  2. In-Mission Daily Tracking & Hands-Free Voice Assistant: During the mission, astronauts log daily visual symptoms, mental stress levels, and countermeasure adherence (such as thigh cuffs usage or scopolamine nasal gels). An integrated offline medical voice assistant allows crew members to record symptoms and query health protocols hands-free, reducing cognitive load in microgravity.
  3. Delay-Tolerant Radio Link Simulation: Because reliable high-speed Internet does not exist in deep space, SANS Guardian compresses daily logs into lightweight JSON packets and transmits them to Earth via a simulated radio link built on MQTT, featuring local offline queuing to handle signal loss, noise, and transmission delays.
  4. Real-Time Dashboards & Post-Mission Reports: Flight surgeons on Earth monitor crew trends through a consolidated dashboard with automated risk alerts, while end-of-mission analytics generate comprehensive individual and crew-wide medical reports.

Benefits and Expected Impact

  • Early Intervention: Shifts astronaut healthcare from reactive post-flight treatment to proactive, early in-flight detection, preventing irreversible ocular damage (such as optic disc edema and globe flattening).
  • Operational Autonomy: Empowers crews on future Artemis (Lunar) and Mars missions to track health and receive voice-guided medical support even during communication blackouts with Earth.
  • Accelerated Space Medicine Research: Standardizes longitudinal pre-, in-, and post-flight datasets, creating a structured demonstrator ready to be trained on real clinical datasets from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).

Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Backend & Predictive Engine: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite / SQLAlchemy, and Scikit-learn (for the SANS risk estimation demonstrator).
  • Frontend & Dashboards: React (for both the astronaut interface and the Earth-based Flight Surgeon monitoring console).
  • Voice Assistant (Offline-First): OpenAI Whisper / Faster-Whisper (Speech-to-Text) and local Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesis.
  • Space Communication Simulation: MQTT protocol (paho-mqtt) to simulate low-bandwidth, delay-tolerant radio packet transmission and offline message buffering.
  • AI Assistance: Claude and Gemini were used to assist with software architecture design, code structuring, data schema validation, and scientific documentation synthesis.

What Makes Our Project Creative

Rather than treating medical tracking as a standard cloud-based health app, SANS Guardian is engineered specifically around the harsh physical realities of spaceflight:

  • Space-Constraint Engineering: Combining hands-free voice interaction (for floating, screen-limited environments) with an MQTT delay-tolerant radio queue directly mirrors real deep-space telemetry constraints.
  • Holistic Mind-Vision Approach: Connecting neuro-ocular fluid-shift risks (SANS) with daily psychological stress and countermeasure adherence offers a unified view of crew readiness rather than isolated metrics.

Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Zero-Connectivity & Latency: Designing an offline-first architecture capable of surviving prolonged signal blackouts without data loss.
  • Crew Workload & Ergonomics: Minimizing manual typing through voice-assisted logging so daily check-ins take seconds rather than minutes.
  • Scientific Grounding: Aligning all tracked biomarkers, risk thresholds, and countermeasures (B-vitamins, thigh cuffs, vestibular adaptation) with official findings from the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and NASA OSDR.
